## The question

[A difficulty in understanding the proof of theorem 4.1 in chapter3 in Israel Gohberg.](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2592061/a-difficulty-in-understanding-the-proof-of-theorem-4-1-in-chapter3-in-israel-goh), asked by [Emptymind](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/417020/emptymind) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2018-01-04; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> The proof is given in the following pictures:
>
> [![enter image description here][q-1]][q-1]
> [![enter image description here][q-2]][q-2]
> [![enter image description here][q-3]][q-3]
>
> Could not calculate the details of how equation(1) come, could anyone help me in doing so please? 
>
>
>
>   [q-1]: mlHHf.png
>   [q-2]: 7Iidt.png
>   [q-3]: N0uHz.png
:::

It's the old multiply-and-divide-the-same thing trick:
$$\left<A(x+y),x+y\right>
   =\left<A\left(\frac{x+y}{\Vert x+y\Vert}\right),\frac{x+y}{\Vert x+y\Vert}\right>\Vert x+y\Vert^2$$
The inner product is of the form $\left<Au,u\right>$ with $\Vert u \Vert =1$, so it's $\leq m$.  So
$$\left<A(x+y),x+y\right> \leq m \Vert x+y\Vert^2$$
Similarly,
$$\left<A(x-y),x-y\right> \leq m \Vert x-y\Vert^2$$
Add them together and use the parallelogram law.
